_notes: Main frame of the mini-pilot (goal C1, task #61). Equal to abstract_v2 except: (a) the system message is the identity card alone (no 'You are a participant in a decision-making experiment. The following describes you:'); (b) the isolated question gives a fixed round ('This is round {round_no} of {rounds}.', round from the config, isolated_round_no, default 5) instead of 'neither the first nor the last round' (isolated_frame fixed_round; one_shot and repeated are not offered by this frame). Rules text unchanged, A2.1 (f) labels included. Adds the two rule-comprehension questions of goal C4 (wording to be approved by the user). Format: frames/SCHEMA.md.
name: abstract_v3
description: Abstract public goods frame of the mini-pilot: card as the whole system message, isolated question at a fixed round, two rule-comprehension questions.

rules.text: - A group has {n} players: you and {n_others} others. Players cannot communicate.
- The game is played in rounds; this question is about one round.
- The same {n} players stay together for all {rounds} rounds.
- In every round each player receives {endowment} points.
- Each player then decides how many of these points (a whole number from 0 to {endowment}) to contribute to a group project. Points that are not contributed stay with the player.
- Every point contributed to the project yields {mpcr} points for each of the {n} players. Your earnings from the project in a round are therefore:
- Your total earnings in a round are the points you kept plus your earnings from the project:
{endowment} - (your contribution) + {mpcr} x (sum of all {n} players' contributions)

- After the contributions of a round are revealed, each player may assign punishment points (0 to {max_punish}) to each other player. Each point assigned costs the assigning player {punish_cost} point(s) and reduces the earnings of the receiving player by {punish_impact} points. A player is told only the total number of punishment points received, not who assigned them.
- After each round you are told every player's contribution and your own earnings.

history.empty:
HISTORY
This is the first round; there is no history yet.
round: Your earnings from the project: {project_share}. Your total earnings this round: {round_earnings}.
round_P: Punishment points you assigned: {punish_given} (cost to you: {cost_paid}).

contribute:
ROUND {round_no} of {rounds}. You are {me}. All players decide at the same time, without seeing each other's choice for this round.
How many of your {endowment} points do you contribute to the group project? (a whole number from 0 to {endowment})
punish:
ROUND {round_no} of {rounds}, punishment step. You are {me}.
This round: {contributions} Your earnings from the project this round: {project_share}. Your total earnings this round (before punishment): {earnings}.
You may now assign punishment points (0 to {max_punish}) to each other player. A point costs you {punish_cost} and reduces the receiving player's earnings by {punish_impact}. Your total cost may not exceed your total earnings this round, so you can assign at most {max_points} points in total. All players decide at the same time.

fixed_round.question:
QUESTION
This is round {round_no} of {rounds}. In the previous round the other {n_others} players of your group contributed, on average, {others_mean} points each.
How many of your {endowment} points do you contribute to the group project in this round? (a whole number from 0 to {endowment})

questions.text: Suppose that in a round you contribute {own} points and the other {n_others} players contribute {other_1}, {other_2} and {other_3} points. What are your total earnings in that round?

Suppose that the contributions of the other players stay the same. If you contribute {delta} more points to the group project, by how much do your own total earnings in that round change? Give a negative number if they go down.

response.rationale_description: One or two sentences on why you chose this.
response.punishment_description: Punishment points per other player, keyed by player number.
